findings.element: shell.css --track-* ladder against every font-size in b.css
findings.problem: The ladder is declared as size-bound (body = sans 15-20, head = sans 24-38, title = 48, display = 96/148) but it is applied by hand, per component, so it does not hold. Measured across 11 states x 4 widths: 24px sans renders at BOTH -0.015em (.b-title at desk) and -0.03em (.b-dayNowTitle); 30px sans renders at BOTH -0.015em (.b-when at desk) and -0.03em (.b-endedTitle) - the exact defect the ladder comment says it was created to end. Eight components set 15/17px sans at 0em with no tracking at all (.b-gapNote, .b-behindNote, .b-dayNote, .b-bubble, .b-undoAct, .b-emptyBody, .b-endedBody, .b-pressBody) while every other 15/17px string carries -0.015em; on the flagship owner screen 'Wedding day at The Orchard' (-0.015em) and 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' (0em) are the same size, 40px apart, at two different letterfits. .b-step sets 15px mono at 0em where the ladder says mono figures take 0.04em. And in the whole min-width:701px block, seven declarations raise a size and exactly one (.b-pressTitle) re-tracks it - so .b-title goes 17 to 24px, .b-when 20 to 30px and .b-emptyTitle 38 to 64px all still wearing the phone's tracking, and 64px ends up running at the 24-38 step. The automated gate checks the size ramp and the leading; it does not check that a size wears its declared track, so none of this is visible to it.
findings.fix: Stop declaring letter-spacing per component. Add utility classes to shell.css bound to the ramp - .t-11/.t-12 (label), .t-15/.t-17/.t-20 (body), .t-24/.t-30/.t-38 (head), .t-48 (title), .t-64/.t-96/.t-148 (display) - each setting font-size and its ladder tracking together, and have render-b.js apply the size class rather than b.css setting font-size. Where a component must stay a class, give every font-size declaration in b.css a letter-spacing on the same line: add letter-spacing: var(--track-body) to .b-gapNote, .b-behindNote, .b-dayNote, .b-bubble, .b-undoAct, .b-emptyBody, .b-endedBody and .b-pressBody; add letter-spacing: var(--track-data) to .b-step; and in the min-width:701px block add letter-spacing: var(--track-head) to the .b-title and .b-when rules, var(--track-title) to .b-emptyTitle (or declare a seventh step at -0.04em if 64px is to keep its own), and var(--track-display) to .b-dayNames. Then extend audit.mjs: for every rendered element assert computed letterSpacing/fontSize equals the step the ramp assigns that size, and fail when one size renders at two tracks.

findings.element: .b-stepRead - the date readout in the owner editor
findings.problem: This is the string round 2 was built around and it is about 2px too wide for the rail it lives in. Driven at 1440 and 1280 the readout box is 326px and 'Saturday 8 August 2026 . in 23 days' at 15px Geist Mono with 0.04em tracking needs roughly 328px, so it wraps to two lines and widows the word 'days' - the unit of the very number the owner is changing - onto a line of its own. Press -7 twice and the string shortens to 'Saturday 25 July 2026 . in 9 days', the block collapses from 45px to 23px, and every control below it moves 22px: the Shown/Hidden switch goes from y=814 to y=792, Done and Delete this moment from y=862 to y=840. Press +7 and they move back down. Same behaviour at 390. It is stable only at 768, where the sheet is full width, which is why nothing caught it - interaction-check asserts the steppers themselves do not move under the pointer, and they do not; everything underneath them does. min-height is auto on this element, so nothing reserves the second line.
findings.fix: Two changes to .b-stepRead in b.css. First, take it off mono: it is an English sentence, not a field - set font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: var(--track-body); and keep the .num class for tabular figures. That buys roughly 70px and makes the string fit one line at every width down to 320. Second, reserve the fallback anyway: min-height: 46px (two lines at 15px/1.5) plus text-wrap: balance, so a longer month or a longer locale can never move the Done button again. If the machine register is wanted on the figures, wrap only the day count in a span carrying font-family: var(--mono) inside the sans sentence.

findings.element: .b-behindNote (the folded past) and .b-note (the revocation note on publish)
findings.problem: Three prose blocks declare a measure - .b-emptyBody at 34ch, .b-endedBody at 40ch, .b-pressBody at 46ch - and the two carrying the most meaning declare none. At 1280 and 1440 .b-behindNote renders '2 done, the last of them 18 April. One thing is not going ahead.' as a single 76-character line 644px wide at 15px, and on the received desk surface 76 characters across 642px. That sentence is the whole of the past by the lock's own decision, and it is set at nearly double the measure of every other paragraph in the file. Worse, .b-note under the publish buttons runs 'You can turn the link off at any time. Anyone holding it then sees that it has ended.' as one 85-character line at 13px across 684px - the longest measure and the smallest type on the same screen, which is the combination the eye loses its place in. The audit gate has no measure check, so both pass.
findings.fix: Add max-width: 46ch to .b-behindNote and max-width: 52ch to .b-note in b.css, alongside the text-wrap: pretty each already carries. Both sit in normal flow with left-aligned siblings, so no other geometry moves. While there, put the same 46ch ceiling on .b-gapNote for the desk case - it is 34 characters in the fixture but it is owner-authored copy with nothing stopping it.

findings.problem: 11px mono uppercase at 0.16em is the most repeated typographic gesture in the lab - 508 rendered instances across the state set - and it is doing three unrelated jobs at one identical setting. On every owner row the date 'SAT 1 AUG' (a fact) and the visibility control 'SHOWN' (a button) sit stacked in the same family, size, case, tracking and ink; at rest nothing tells a reader which of those two lines can be pressed. On the unfurl card - the frame most guests see before they ever open the plan - 'MARA & FINN' and 'DAYS TO SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER 2026' are both 11px mono uppercase at fore-62, separated only by 0.20em against 0.16em, a 0.04em difference no reader can perceive. So the couple's own date, the emotional payload of the whole artifact, is set as a 31-character machine stamp that is the widest line on the card, while the number above it gets 48px against the 148px it gets in the app. The card inverts the hierarchy the product spent its entire scale on.
findings.fix: Split the step by role rather than by tracking. (1) .b-grab: color: var(--fore-46) at rest with text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--fore-16); text-underline-offset: 3px, keeping the existing hover and focus promotion to var(--fore) - a control then reads as a control at rest while the date stays a plain fact at fore-62. (2) .b-ogDate: take it off the label step entirely - font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: var(--track-body); text-transform: none; color: var(--fore-72) - and render it sentence case as '79 days to Saturday 3 October 2026', so the card reads number then sentence rather than stamp, number, stamp. (3) Raise .b-ogNum from 48px to 64px with letter-spacing: var(--track-display) so the card previews the hierarchy of the surface it links to.

findings.problem: Three bad breaks, each in a place that repeats. .b-measureHead is 62px wide on phone and its string is 'days away', so the column head the entire measure hangs from renders as 'DAYS / AWAY' with a one-word second line at 390, 768 and 1280 - it is in every phone frame in the shot set, the one screen the brief says decides. On the A4 keepsake, .b-title has -webkit-line-clamp but no text-wrap: balance, so 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' and 'Choose the evening music' both break with a single word alone on line 2 - two of the seven rows on the printed sheet. And .b-when at sheet width breaks the ceremonial date as 'Saturday 3 / October 2026', splitting the day number from its month on the object the couple keeps.
findings.fix: (1) Give .b-measureHead white-space: nowrap and widen its phone lane: .b-measureHead width 62px to 76px, .b-measure padding-left 96px to 110px, .b-rail left 76px to 90px, .b-item left 96px to 110px, .b-away left -96px to -110px and width 62px to 76px, so the head sits on one line at 390. (2) Add text-wrap: balance to .b-title. (3) In render-b.js, build the long date with a non-breaking space between the day number and the month (replace the space after the day digits in F.fmt.longYear output with U+00A0) so 'Saturday 3 October 2026' can only break after 'Saturday' or before '2026'.

biggestWin: The scale does hierarchy on its own - two weights, no colour, and it still reads. The countdown at 96 and 148px Geist Mono with a hand-set -0.05em optical inset so the largest object on the page hangs flush to its column; a 24px sans row title carrying the person's words above an 11px mono date, so the human string always outranks the machine string; tabular figures wired through one .num utility on every number that changes under the reader, so the count never twitches as it counts; word-safe clamping that keeps the full sentence in the title attribute and in the accessibility tree and re-runs on fonts.ready and on resize; leading declared on every block and never left at normal. Those are the parts a studio would keep untouched, and they are why this is a 7.4 rather than a 6.
